0.name: ACS 5-Year 2024, table S1901 — median household income by census tract
0.note: On disk. scripts/pairwise_socioeconomic_regression.py reads the same file, so the 2 analyses share one income source. The geoid is the 11-digit tract code and it matches the tract layer for 100% of tracts.

1.name: ACS 5-Year 2024, table B01003 — total population by census tract
1.note: Weights for the NTA and community-district aggregation. You cannot average medians, so those 2 layers report a population-weighted mean of the tract medians, not a median.

2.name: NYC Atomic Polygons
2.note: NOT needed. Atomic polygons would be necessary only if a census tract split across an NTA or a community district. Checked 2026-08-12: every one of the 2,325 tracts puts its interior point in exactly 1 NTA and exactly 1 community district, and no tract falls in 2 polygons. Keep this entry so the next reader knows the check happened and why the source stays unused.

3.name: NYC Building Footprints (BUILDING)
3.note: On disk, pulled 2026-04-12 by data/geo/download_nyc_buildings.py. 1,082,872 footprints and 99.1% carry a usable year; the source writes 0 for an unknown year and _proxies drops it. FacDB gives each unit a BIN, thus this is a key join and not a spatial one. WARNING: a year is NOT oriented. Every other proxy points 'higher is better', so a positive value means agreement. A positive value here says the model calls a NEWER unit better, which is a finding and not a test.

4.name: DOB Violations
4.note: A fault that the Department of Buildings recorded against this building. FacDB gives 96.8% of the libraries a BIN, thus this is a key join and not a spatial one. The source holds more than 2,000,000 rows, so the query sends the BIN list of this case to the server and groups there. A category that ends in ACTIVE is an open violation. WARNING: a count rises when a building gets worse, thus _proxies_buildings applies a sign of -1 and the exported value points 'higher is better'.

5.name: DOB ECB Violations
5.note: An Environmental Control Board violation carries a fine, thus it marks a fault that reached a hearing. The status is ACTIVE or RESOLVE. The export adds these counts to the DOB counts, and proxy_source names the 2 ids together.

6.name: DOB Permit Issuance
6.note: A permit says that somebody spent money on this building, thus it is a positive measure and it needs no sign. The count is over the distinct job number and not over the permit rows, because 1 job takes an initial permit, a renewal, and 1 permit for each trade. Job types A1, A2, and A3 only: a new building and a demolition are not investments in the building the model looked at. WARNING: issuance_date holds 2 shapes, MM/DD/YYYY and an ISO timestamp, thus the server cannot filter the year and the module filters it in pandas.

7.name: DOB NOW: Safety - Facades Compliance Filings (FISP)
7.note: NOT used as a proxy. Local Law 11 applies to a building of more than 6 storeys, and a branch library is low. Measured 2026-08-31: 28 of the 236 library BINs (11.9%) carry any filing, and 27 carry one since 2016. A correlation over 12% of the case would describe the tall libraries alone. _proxies_buildings.facade_status_by_bin builds the frame for a reader who wants it, and no export row comes from it.
